## Answers

**h01** — component: `s3presign.Runner` (server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16) via `CheckAndPresign` (runner.go:47), which re-presigns any S3 object URL whose `LastPresignedTime` is within 4 days of its 5-day expiry. Schedule: every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, runner.go:27), run via `Run`'s ticker loop (runner.go:29-41), plus one immediate `RunOnce` at startup. Wiring: `server/server.go:162-169` inside `startBackgroundRunners`, called from `Start` (server.go:129).

**h02** — Delivery function: `webhook.Post` — internal/webhook/webhook.go:120 (invoked by the async workers started in `init()` at webhook.go:42-55, which pull from `asyncPostQueue` and call `Post`, fed by `PostAsync` at webhook.go:184). Protection: `safeDialContext` (webhook.go:59-77), used as the `http.Transport.DialContext` of the shared `safeClient` (webhook.go:32-37) — it resolves the hostname and rejects any IP in a reserved/private range via `isReservedIP` (internal/webhook/validate.go:44-54), covering loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/cloud IMDS, and IPv6 equivalents (validate.go:14-23). `ValidateURL` (validate.go:62) additionally rejects bad URLs up front at webhook-creation time (server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182).

**h03** — Abstraction package: `internal/idp` (internal/idp/idp.go — `IdentityProviderUserInfo` struct). Concrete implementation shipped: `internal/idp/oauth2` (oauth2.go — `IdentityProvider` struct with `ExchangeToken`/`UserInfo`, constructed at server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:121).

**h04** — No. The only import of `store/db/mysql` in non-test code is `store/db/db.go:8`, and the only call to `mysql.NewDB` anywhere in the codebase is `store/db/db.go:22` inside the driver-selection factory `NewDBDriver`. `find_references` for `NewDB` across the repo returns exactly the three factory calls (sqlite/mysql/postgres) plus the three package definitions and two sqlite-only test helpers — no other mysql construction site exists.

**h05** — Explicit Go code (not a DB-level cascade/trigger). `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96,102` (`deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`, `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`) run `DELETE FROM reaction WHERE content_id IN (...)` and `DELETE FROM reaction WHERE creator_id = ?` inside the `DeleteUser` transaction (sqlite/user_delete.go:29,92-127), removing reactions both by the deleted user and on the user's deleted memos. Equivalent code exists in `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:29` and `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:29`. Checked the migration SQL (store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99) — the `reaction` table has no `ON DELETE CASCADE` foreign-key clause, so this is app-level cleanup, not a DB rule.

**h06** — Handlers: `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` (memo_service.go:70, via DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook at memo_service.go:157), `APIV1Service.DeleteMemo` (memo_service.go:518, via DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook at memo_service.go:562), `APIV1Service.CreateMemoComment` (memo_service_comments.go:20, via DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook at memo_service_comments.go:119), and `APIV1Service.UpdateMemo` (memo_service.go:401, via `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`→`DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` at memo_update_helpers.go:67). Convergence function: `webhook.Post` — internal/webhook/webhook.go:120 (all four dispatch methods call `webhook.PostAsync`, whose queue workers all call `Post`).

```

```
(Route: `GET /users/:identifier/avatar`. On a private instance, `getCurrentUser`→`authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` gates access first; `store.Store.GetUser` also checks `userCache` before falling through to `ListUsers`/driver SQL.)

**h08** — Declarers of `RunOnce`: `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` (server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27) and `s3presign.Runner.RunOnce` (server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43).
- `s3presign.Runner.RunOnce` — invoked from production code: `server/server.go:163` and internally from `Run` at s3presign/runner.go:36.
- `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` — not invoked anywhere in the codebase (no production caller, no test caller found); its constructor `memopayload.NewRunner` is also never called. It is effectively dead/unwired code — only the free function `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (used by the Runner) is called elsewhere, from `memo_service.go:108,447`.

**h09** — 8 total declarations of `Close`: `SSEHub.Close` (server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99), `cache.Cache.Close` (store/cache/cache.go:187), `mysql.DB.Close` (store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47), `postgres.DB.Close` (store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46), `sqlite.DB.Close` (store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67), `Store.Close` (store/store.go:72), plus two test-only helpers in store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:200,282.
Invoked by non-test server code: `Store.Close` — called from `Server.Shutdown` (server/server.go:146); `Store.Close` in turn calls the driver's `Close` (whichever of mysql/postgres/sqlite is active, store/store.go:78) and the three `cache.Cache.Close` (store/store.go:74-76). `SSEHub.Close` — called from `Server.closeLongLivedConnections` (server/server.go:206).

**h10** — `store.Store.GetMemo` (store/memo.go:120) is among the highest fan-in symbols under `internal/`-adjacent server code per `[ArchMap query]`, but the graph's clear #1 fan-in symbol overall in Go code is `store.User` (struct, 85 inbound references, store/user.go:29) — a type, not a function/method. Restricting to a genuine function/method: `postgres.placeholder` (store/db/postgres/common.go:16) has 105 inbound edges but is dialect-scoped helper, not under `internal/`. Within `internal/`, none of the hotspot leaders live there — `[ArchMap query]` shows no `internal/`-rooted symbol in the global top 20 (all leaders are in `store`, `proto/gen`, `web/src`, or `server/router/api/v1`). The closest `internal/`-declared function by measured fan-in is `filter.AppendConditions` (internal/filter/helpers.go:9), called from 6 sites (3 driver `ListMemoRelations`-adjacent call sites via `CompileToStatement`, plus attachment/memo list paths across mysql/postgres/sqlite) — cannot determine a single internal/-scoped symbol with clearly higher fan-in than this from the tool's ranking, since [ArchMap query] does not restrict to internal/ and no internal/ symbol surfaced in its global top-20.

**h11** — 1st: `store.User` (store/user.go:29) — referenced from ~27 files spanning server/router/api/v1 (user_service*.go, auth*, memo_mention_helpers, memo_service_converter, fileserver, rss), server/auth, server/notification, and all three store/db/* drivers (per `[ArchMap query]`). 2nd: `store.Memo` (store/memo.go:35) — referenced from ~18 files across server/notification, server/router/api/v1 (several memo-adjacent files), server/runner/memopayload, server/router/rss, and the three store/db/* drivers.

**h12** — Concrete method: `sqlite.DB.CreateMemo` (store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16), which runs `INSERT INTO \`memo\` (...) ... RETURNING \`id\`, \`created_ts\`, \`updated_ts\`, \`row_status\`` (memo.go:41-42). Determination: traced the driver-selection factory `store/db/db.go:14-32` (`NewDBDriver`, switches on `profile.Driver`), then confirmed the default value is `"sqlite"` both in `viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")` and the CLI flag default `rootCmd.PersistentFlags().String("driver", "sqlite", ...)` in cmd/memos/main.go:122,130 — so with no db flags supplied, the sqlite branch (and hence `sqlite.DB.CreateMemo`) is what executes, not the equivalent mysql/postgres candidates.

**h13** — Impl: the unexported `service` struct in internal/markdown/markdown.go:58, wrapping a `goldmark.Markdown`. Construction: `markdown.NewService(...)` (markdown.go:85), called at three sites — `v1.NewAPIV1Service` (server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48, with tag+mention extensions), `rss.NewRSSService`'s caller at server/server.go:85 (reuses `apiV1Service.MarkdownService`), and `memopayload.NewRunner`'s (unused-in-prod) constructor. Interface holders: `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35), `rss.RSSService.MarkdownService` (server/router/rss/rss.go:45), and `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` (server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16) — all typed as `markdown.Service`.

**h14** — Computation site: `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74), which calls `markdownService.ExtractAll(content)` and writes `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property`. Triggers: `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` (memo_service.go:108) and `APIV1Service.UpdateMemo` when the `content` field-mask path is set (memo_service.go:447); also a batch backfill path in `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` (runner.go:52), though that Runner is currently unwired into server startup (see h08). Extracted properties: `Tags` (from `#tag` parsing) and `Property` (a `*storepb.MemoPayload_Property` of boolean/derived flags) via `markdown.Service.ExtractAll`, both computed from raw memo content rather than user-supplied.

**h15** — At least six distinct enforcement sites:
- `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:55,63` (GetMemo/ListMemos read path)
- `server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30,38,83` (reactions)
- `server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:214,222` (memo attachments listing)
- `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:445,451` (attachment access)

**r01** — Premise is wrong: there is no Redis. The cache layer is an in-process, in-memory cache (`store/cache/cache.go`, a `sync.Map`-backed `Cache` with a background TTL-eviction goroutine, cache.go:66-90). It is instantiated inside `store.New` (store/store.go:38-61) with `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute` (store.go:41), used for three named caches: `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` (store.go:27-29). So: user entries get a 10-minute TTL, and there is no Redis connection anywhere in the codebase to configure.

**r02** — Premise is wrong: no rate-limiting middleware exists anywhere in this codebase. Text search for "rate limit" across the graph returns a certified miss (0/7293 symbols), and `server/server.go`'s middleware stack registers only `middleware.Recover()` and CORS (server.go:51-52) — no throttling/limiter middleware is registered at any router (api/v1, fileserver, frontend, rss, mcp).
